cases.explain: «Старый граф» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: The old count went home, and Natásha and Pétya promised to return very soon, but as it was still early the hunt went farther. At midday they put the hounds into a ravine thickly overgrown with young trees. Nikoláy standing in a fallow field could see all his whips.

cases.sentence: В середине дня гончих пустили в поросший молодым ___ овраг.
cases.explain: «частым лесом» — the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: The old count went home, and Natásha and Pétya promised to return very soon, but as it was still early the hunt went farther. At midday they put the hounds into a ravine thickly overgrown with young trees. Nikoláy standing in a fallow field could see all his whips.

cases.sentence: Только что завели гончих, Николай услыхал ___ известной ему собаки — Волторна; другие собаки присоединились к нему, то замолкая, то опять принимаясь гнать.
cases.explain: «редкий гон» — the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: Facing him lay a field of winter rye, there his own huntsman stood alone in a hollow behind a hazel bush. The hounds had scarcely been loosed before Nikoláy heard one he knew, Voltórn, giving tongue at intervals; other hounds joined in, now pausing and now again giving tongue. A moment later he heard a cry from the wooded ravine that a fox had been found, and the whole pack, joining together, rushed along the ravine toward the ryefield and away from Nikoláy.

cases.sentence: Он видел скачущих выжлятников в ___ по краям поросшего оврага, видел даже собак, и всякую секунду ждал того, что на той стороне, на зеленях, покажется лисица.
cases.explain: «красных шапках» — after the preposition «в», for location or topic.
cases.translation: He saw the whips in their red caps galloping along the edge of the ravine, he even saw the hounds, and was expecting a fox to show itself at any moment on the ryefield opposite.

cases.sentence: К собакам подскакали два охотника: один в ___, другой, чужой, в зеленом кафтане.
cases.explain: «красной шапке» — after the preposition «в», for location or topic.
cases.translation: The huntsman standing in the hollow moved and loosed his borzois, and Nikoláy saw a queer, short-legged red fox with a fine brush going hard across the field. The borzois bore down on it. … Now they drew close to the fox which began to dodge between the field in sharper and sharper curves, trailing its brush, when suddenly a strange white borzoi dashed in followed by a black one, and everything was in confusion; the borzois formed a star-shaped figure, scarcely swaying their bodies and with tails turned away from the center of the group. Two huntsmen galloped up to the dogs; one in a red cap, the other, a stranger, in a green coat.

cases.sentence: Оттуда же раздался звук рога — ___ драки.
cases.explain: «условленный сигнал» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: The huntsmen got the fox, but stayed there a long time without strapping it to the saddle. Their horses, bridled and with high saddles, stood near them and there too the dogs were lying. The huntsmen waved their arms and did something to the fox. Then from that spot came the sound of a horn, with the signal agreed on in case of a fight.

cases.sentence: Из-за опушки выехал дравшийся охотник с лисицей в тороках и подъехал к ___.
cases.explain: «молодому барину» — after the preposition «к», the dative marks the indirect object or recipient.
cases.translation: Nikoláy dismounted, and with Natásha and Pétya, who had ridden up, stopped near the hounds, waiting to see how the matter would end. Out of the bushes came the huntsman who had been fighting and rode toward his young master, with the fox tied to his crupper. While still at a distance he took off his cap and tried to speak respectfully, but he was pale and breathless and his face was angry. One of his eyes was black, but he probably was not even aware of it.

cases.sentence: Он озлобленно-взволнованный ехал теперь к нему, крепко сжимая арапник в руке, в ___ на самые решительные и опасные действия против своего врага.
cases.explain: «полной готовности» — after the preposition «в», for location or topic.
cases.translation: Nikoláy, though he had never seen Ilágin, with his usual absence of moderation in judgment, hated him cordially from reports of his arbitrariness and violence, and regarded him as his bitterest foe. He rode in angry agitation toward him, firmly grasping his whip and fully prepared to take the most resolute and desperate steps to punish his enemy.

cases.sentence: Вместо врага Николай нашел в Илагине представительного, учтивого барина, особенно желавшего познакомиться с ___.
cases.explain: «молодым графом» — after the preposition «с», the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: Instead of an enemy, Nikoláy found in Ilágin a stately and courteous gentleman who was particularly anxious to make the young count’s acquaintance. Having ridden up to Nikoláy, Ilágin raised his beaver cap and said he much regretted what had occurred and would have the man punished who had allowed himself to seize a fox hunted by someone else’s borzois. He hoped to become better acquainted with the count and invited him to draw his covert.

cases.sentence: Дядюшка, Ростов, Илагин поглядывали тайком на ___, стараясь, чтобы другие этого не замечали, и с беспокойством отыскивали между этими собаками соперниц своим собакам.
cases.explain: «чужих собак» — after the preposition «на», the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: The way to Iligin’s upland was across the fields. The hunt servants fell into line. The masters rode together. “Uncle,” Rostóv, and Ilágin kept stealthily glancing at one another’s dogs, trying not to be observed by their companions and searching uneasily for rivals to their own borzois.
